# Engine names the Unreal seed assumes

<!-- Generated by `npm run unreal:symbols -- --write` from engine-symbols.json. Do not edit. -->

Every engine name the Unreal seed (unreal/) and the stand-ins its tests compile it against (tests/tools/unreal-standin/) assume, each checked against Epic's public documentation, or, for a rule of the C++ language itself, against the C++20 working draft. The seed has never been built by the engine; this register says how far the public record supports each assumption, and what only a build can settle.

**How it was checked.** Epic's documentation at dev.epicgames.com: the guides of the current version, and the C++ API reference of Unreal Engine 5.8, or of 5.5 and 5.7 where the 5.8 page leaves a detail out. The seed targets Unreal Engine 5.9, whose API reference was not published when this was checked. The reference prints signatures without default arguments, does not document macros, and drops a trailing const in its class tables. Epic's engine source is not public, so no header was read. Where an assumption is a rule of the C++ language rather than of the engine, it is checked against the C++20 working draft (N4861, in the cplusplus/draft repository on GitHub), the standard Epic's coding standard says the engine builds with.

Checked on 2026-11-15. The register, [engine-symbols.json](engine-symbols.json), holds for each name the files that use it, what is assumed, the page and the quoted passage. `npm run unreal:symbols` fails when the seed or a stand-in uses an engine name that is not entered; with `--online` it opens every page again and looks for each passage.

| Status | Names | Meaning |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| verified | 188 | The quoted passage, on the page named, states or shows what is assumed: the name and, for a function, its parameters or the behaviour relied on. |
| partly | 6 | The name is documented but something the seed or a stand-in relies on is not: a default argument, a value's spelling, an include that brings a name in. |
| unverified | 1 | No public page was found that shows it. |
| contradicted | 1 | A public page says otherwise. |
| all | 196 | |

## What the public record does not settle

These are for the first build in the engine to settle. Each row says what is missing. 3 of them are corroborated: a public project built against Unreal Engine 5 uses the name as the seed does. That is evidence, not Epic's word, and leaves each status as it is.

| Name | Status | Page | What is assumed, and what is missing |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FPaths::ProjectDir (the folder of the .uproject)` | partly | [FPaths::ProjectDir](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/API/Runtime/Core/FPaths/ProjectDir?application_version=5.8) | ProjectDir() is the folder that holds Tervain.uproject, so the default data directory ../data is the repository's data folder. The stand-in returns it with a trailing slash; the seed relies on neither that nor whether it is absolute, because it passes the result through FPaths::Combine and ConvertRelativePathToFull. The reference says the base directory of the current project, "usually a subdirectory of the installation root directory", and Epic's page on managing game code draws each project folder holding its Binaries, Config and .uproject file. That ProjectDir() returns that folder is the plain reading but is not stated. If it does not, the seed logs where it looked for the tuning file and asks for the data directory to be set in Project Settings. |
| `Logging/LogMacros.h` | partly | [FMsg](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/API/Runtime/Core/FMsg?application_version=5.8) | The logging macros are available after including "Logging/LogMacros.h" (module Core). The header holds FMsg, whose struct "contains functions for messaging with tools or debug logs" (Logf among them), and the Core module page lists the include path. The API reference does not document macros, so that UE_LOG, DECLARE_LOG_CATEGORY_EXTERN and DEFINE_LOG_CATEGORY come from this header is not shown, and the logging guide names no header for them. |
| `IMPLEMENT_PRIMARY_GAME_MODULE` | contradicted | [Gameplay Modules in Unreal Engine](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/gameplay-modules-in-unreal-engine) | IMPLEMENT_PRIMARY_GAME_MODULE(ModuleImplClass, ModuleName, GameName) takes three arguments: the seed writes (FDefaultGameModuleImpl, Tervain, "Tervain"). The only Epic page found that shows the macro gives it two arguments, the module name and the game name, with no implementation class. That page reads as dated (its Build.cs sample takes TargetInfo and it speaks of an OutExtraModuleNames array), and the newer module pages show IMPLEMENT_MODULE(FDefaultModuleImpl, ModuleTest) with the class first; the API reference documents FDefaultGameModuleImpl, the class the seed passes first, as the "Default minimal module class for gameplay modules". So the three-argument form may well be the current one, but no page fetched shows it and the API reference does not document macros. Check against Modules/ModuleManager.h in the engine at the first build. The requirement itself ("At least one module in your game must be registered using IMPLEMENT_PRIMARY_GAME_MODULE") is confirmed. Corroborated: [CARLA's game module, on its ue5-dev branch (the Unreal Engine 5.5 version of CARLA, per its README)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/carla-simulator/carla/ue5-dev/Unreal/CarlaUnreal/Source/CarlaUnreal/CarlaUnreal.cpp) has `IMPLEMENT_PRIMARY_GAME_MODULE( FDefaultGameModuleImpl, CarlaUnreal, "CarlaUnreal" );`. |
| `Primitive types and TEXT from CoreMinimal.h` | partly | [Include What You Use (IWYU) for Unreal Engine Programming](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/include-what-you-use-iwyu-for-unreal-engine-programming) | Including CoreMinimal.h is enough for int32, uint8, uint32, TCHAR and TEXT; every other engine name the seed uses comes from its own header. The page says CoreTypes.h holds the typedefs for primitive types and is included first by most engine headers, and the Core module page speaks of "the core types included in CoreMinimal.h" (TIsUECoreType) without listing them. That CoreMinimal.h includes CoreTypes.h is not stated on any page fetched. The same IWYU page gives the rule the seed follows: every file includes the header of everything it uses. |
| `Containers/UnrealString.h` | partly | [Core](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/API/Runtime/Core?application_version=5.8) | #include "Containers/UnrealString.h" declares FString. The Core module page lists functions that return and take FString under this include path. The FString page itself (5.7 and 5.8) gives the class's file as Containers/UnrealString.h.inl, a part of this header by its name; that including Containers/UnrealString.h declares FString is the long-standing form but is not stated. |
| `UENUM(BlueprintType)` | partly | [Structs in Unreal Engine](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/structs-in-unreal-engine) | BlueprintType exposes an enum to Blueprints. BlueprintType is documented for structs (quoted) and for classes ("Exposes this class as a type that can be used for variables in Blueprints", Class Specifiers). No page fetched lists it as an enum specifier or shows UENUM(BlueprintType): the API reference pages for enums do not print their UENUM line, and Epic's guide examples write UENUM() or UENUM(Meta = (Bitflags)). The seed's enums need it only to show in Blueprints; the C++ and the data tables do not depend on it. |
| `BuildSettingsVersion.Latest` | partly | [Unreal Engine Build Tool Target Reference](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/unreal-engine-build-tool-target-reference) | Latest is a value of the enum BuildSettingsVersion. The property's type is given as BuildSettingsVersion, and the 5.7 release notes write a value of it: "DefaultBuildSettings = BuildSettingsVersion.V6". The target reference names Latest only as DefaultSettingsVersion.Latest, so the spelling BuildSettingsVersion.Latest is not shown anywhere. The same sentence documents the trade-off of Latest: build errors may appear when the engine version changes. Corroborated: [CARLA's game target, on its ue5-dev branch (the Unreal Engine 5.5 version of CARLA, per its README)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/carla-simulator/carla/ue5-dev/Unreal/CarlaUnreal/Source/CarlaUnreal.Target.cs) has `DefaultBuildSettings = BuildSettingsVersion.Latest;`. |
| `EngineIncludeOrderVersion.Latest` | unverified | none found | Latest is a value of the enum EngineIncludeOrderVersion. The target and module references name the type only ("IncludeOrderVersion (EngineIncludeOrderVersion): What version of include order to use when compiling this target"); no page fetched, the 5.5 to 5.8 release notes included, lists its values. Corroborated: [CARLA's game target, on its ue5-dev branch (the Unreal Engine 5.5 version of CARLA, per its README)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/carla-simulator/carla/ue5-dev/Unreal/CarlaUnreal/Source/CarlaUnreal.Target.cs) has `IncludeOrderVersion = EngineIncludeOrderVersion.Latest;`. |
